title: The Enron-Era Tricks Are Back in AI: How These Companies Are Hiding Their Debt | The Weekly Wrap

metadata.title: The Enron-Era Tricks Are Back in AI: How These Companies Are Hiding Their Debt | The Weekly Wrap

summary: The episode warns that higher rates and complex AI financing may expose balance-sheet risks. Eisman distinguishes visible Nvidia vendor financing from Meta's unconsolidated venture, but his interpretation of EY's audit work contradicts the procedures he reads aloud. He also considers agentic commerce, streaming competition and a qualified correction to his earlier short-against-the-box discussion. The rate threshold and market-correction timing are not tightly defined enough for a clean forecast score.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.
framework_points: Trace legal recourse and off-balance-sheet support commitments.
Separate vendor financing from economic end-demand.
Revisit a prior claim when listeners identify a technical problem.
transcript_cautions: The audit interpretation conflicts with the audit procedures read earlier in the same episode.
SIV and VIE terminology is garbled in captions, but the referenced structures are clear.

claims.claim: Meta's Louisiana venture remains outside its balance sheet while Meta retains significant financing and operating exposure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Review control rights, guarantees and maximum-loss disclosure.
claims.qualifications: This confirms nonconsolidation and exposure, not misconduct.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence supports this narrowly stated claim.

evidence.title: Meta Platforms 2025 Form 10-K
evidence.finding: EY describes control tests, review of VIE agreements and an audit of the primary-beneficiary determination. The Louisiana venture is unconsolidated, with $45.95 billion maximum exposure disclosed.

claims.next_check: Review control rights, guarantees and maximum-loss disclosure.

claims.claim: EY's CAM means it did no real independent work and relied on Meta because it wanted the fees.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the spoken interpretation with the actual audit procedures and AS3101.
claims.reason: EY expressly describes controls tests, agreement review and auditing the beneficiary determination. Eisman reads those procedures immediately before claiming they were absent. The asserted fee motive is unproved.

claims.claim: He corrects his short-against-the-box suggestion by invoking the year-end closing and subsequent 60-day holding exception to constructive-sale treatment.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Apply all statutory conditions to an actual position; distinguish reduced price exposure from automatic tax deferral.
claims.qualifications: He describes his own timing hedge and directs listeners to specialist advice; the planned reopening is in 2027.
claims.reason: The cited exception exists, but it additionally requires unreduced risk of loss throughout the 60 days. The original discussion omitted constructive sales and this correction does not fully spell out that third condition.

evidence.title: Publication 550 (2025): Constructive Sales
evidence.finding: Shorting the same appreciated stock generally creates a taxable constructive sale. The closed-transaction exception requires close by 30 days after tax-year-end, 60 days continued ownership and no reduction of risk during those 60 days.

claims.next_check: Apply all statutory conditions to an actual position; distinguish reduced price exposure from automatic tax deferral.

materiality_note: Major theses, forecasts and analytical principles are separated from supporting factual premises. Do not rank the analyst by a raw count of all claims or let small numerical corrections dominate the synthesis. Guest and uncertain-speaker records are excluded from Eisman scoring.
